name: Blind
source:
BLIND isn’t just a novel. It’s a dark, sensual,
dangerous descent into the things we crave but never dare to say out loud.
Ethan, 18, grew up in darkness, literally. Blind for years,
he’s lived under the constant care of two women who orbit him, protect him,
and watch over him in ways they don’t fully admit to themselves.
Day by day, his mood sinks deeper, his body burns hotter,
and his hormones push him toward needs he can’t express on his own.

A psychologist gives them a shocking suggestion: a “release,” a weekly,
intimate intervention meant to calm his spiraling frustration a boundary none of them should cross, yet one all of them secretly imagine.
While the women wrestle with shame, desire, and the thin line between care and temptation,
Ethan hides a secret of his own: his sight is slowly coming back.
Shadows, silhouettes, touches he shouldn’t see, but does. He watches everything.
The tension, the conflict, the desire simmering under every breath, every tremble, every forbidden moment. And no one knows he sees.
